findings: Error & main dispatch alignment (`crates/mori/src/error.rs`, `crates/mori/src/main.rs`, `crates/mori/src/commands/core_io.rs`): `CliError::Operation { code: String, message: String }` is a `thiserror` enum variant with struct fields `code` and `message` (rendered via `#[error("{code}: {message}")]`) and has no `.with_code(...)` builder. `main.rs::main` runs `Cli::parse()`, constructs `Shell`, dispatches `commands::run`, and on `Err(report)` calls `shell.report(&report)` to stderr and returns `ExitCode::FAILURE` (OS exit 1), never emitting a JSON error object or exit 2 (exit 2 comes only from clap parse/validation failures in `Cli::parse()`). Because `core_io::operation` hardcodes `code: "mori::command".into()`, the proposed common unavailable helper in `commands/mod.rs` must construct `CliError::Operation { code: "mori::command::native-unavailable".into(), message: "This mori build has no Midnight support. Rebuild with the native feature enabled.".into() }.into()` directly.

Explicit assessment of `inspect --target` pre-I/O availability policy vs. post-read profile alternative (`crates/mori/src/commands/inspect.rs`, `crates/mori/tests/core_continuations.rs`): In existing default/native `inspect::run`, `core_io::read_source(&args.file)` runs first; if `args.target` is supplied on a `moriarty/2` file, `inspect::run` loads the staged program and returns Core's typed profile refusal (`mori::core::profile`) before reading `--target` (`h16_core_two_inspect_target_refuses_with_core_profile_before_target_read`). The design's policy—having no-native `inspect` with `--target` refuse immediately with `mori::command::native-unavailable` before `read_source(&args.file)` even on `moriarty/2` inputs, while keeping default/native ordering and source-only `inspect` (`args.target.is_none()`) untouched and gating the post-read Core/2 `--target` branch and `core1_refusal()` under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]`—is superior to the post-read profile alternative. The post-read alternative would breach the zero-file-I/O capability boundary by probing/reading `--file` on an unsupported native flag route, surface file-read/size errors before capability refusal on Core/1 or missing paths, and require retaining `core1_refusal()` outside `native`. Gating `h16_core_two_inspect_target_refuses_with_core_profile_before_target_read` under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` and adding a no-native counterpart asserting `mori::command::native-unavailable` before source/target read cleanly preserves both contracts.

Preserving pure argument checks before availability in `intent`, `verify-intent`, and `simulate` (`crates/mori/src/commands/{intent,verify_intent,simulate}.rs`): In `simulate.rs`, clap conflicts (`--resume` vs `--trace`/`--target`/etc., `--logical-cap` vs `--trace`) and `logical_cap` parsing fail with exit 2 before dispatch, and `args.trace` checks `args.target.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| super::core_io::operation("--trace requires --target"))?` before the no-native `run_trace` availability refusal and before any file reads. In `verify_intent.rs`, `match (args.profile, &args.target)` in `run()` already validates `--profile` without `--target` and `--target` without `--profile` before calling `signed(&args, target)`. In `intent.rs`, however, the check that `--profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1` requires both `--target` and `--at` (`let (Some(target), Some(at)) = (&args.target, args.at) else { return Err(super::core_io::operation("--profile moriarty-jubjub-owner-intent/1 requires --target and --at together")); };`) currently sits at the top of `fn signed(...)` (lines 154-158). Implementation must retain that pure `(&args.target, args.at)` check ahead of the no-native `mori::command::native-unavailable` return (either in `intent::run` before calling `signed`, or as the first statement of the no-native `signed` function) so missing `--target`/`--at` under `--profile` still reports the argument error before build availability.

Cargo manifest & 8 SDK dev-dependency optionalization (`crates/mori/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `crates/mori-core/Cargo.toml`): Setting `default = ["native"]`, making `mori-backend`, `mori-ledger`, `futures`, and `rand` optional normal dependencies under `native`, and moving the 8 Midnight crates (`midnight-ledger`, `midnight-base-crypto`, `midnight-coin-structure`, `midnight-onchain-state`, `midnight-onchain-runtime`, `midnight-storage`, `midnight-transient-crypto`, `midnight-serialize`) from unconditional `[dev-dependencies]` to optional normal `[dependencies]` enabled by `native` (leaving `indoc` and `insta` in `[dev-dependencies]`) is required because Cargo does not support optional dev-dependencies. All 8 Midnight crates are already transitive dependencies of `mori-ledger` in default/native builds, `k256` remains unconditional in `mori-core` for legacy `schnorr_bip340`/`ecdsa_secp256k1_sha256` intents, and `Cargo.lock` remains untouched.

Module/helper `#[cfg(feature = "native")]` gating completeness & dead-code prevention (`crates/mori/src/commands/*.rs`): Keeping all clap `Args`, `Command` variants, `ActionInput`, `SignedProfile`, `SigningOutputArgs`, `replay::AuthorizationArgs` (with `present()`), `proof_io::Input`, `call_io::Input`, and `signed_call_io::Input` unconditional preserves identical CLI schemas across builds. To ensure `cargo check/clippy -p mori --no-default-features` compiles cleanly without `dead_code` or `unused_imports` warnings: (a) in `proof_io.rs`, gate `require_new`, `Staging`, `NEXT`, `publish_new`, and their `std::fs`/`std::io`/`std::sync::atomic` imports alongside `Signed`, `Inputs`, `impl Input`, and `tests`; (b) in `compile_call.rs`, gate `validate_shape` (lines 84-119) as well as `artifact_bytes`, `static_text`, `run_static`, `publish_static`, `publish_static_with`, `publish`, and `tests` when no-native `compile_call::run` forwards directly to the unavailable error; (c) in `core_io.rs`, gate `ledger_operation`, `key_export_identity`, `signed_target`, `authority`, `signed_intent`, `key_export_diagnostic_tests`, and `degree_diagnostic_tests`, keeping `read_source`, `read_json`, `program`, `print`, `operation`, and `review_identity` unconditional.

Test target split, mixed Core tests, and frozen CLI oracles (`crates/mori/tests/*.rs`): Marking the 11 native-only integration test targets with `required-features = ["native"]` (or crate-root `#[cfg(feature = "native")]`) and selectively gating native tests in `core_continuations.rs` (`stage_compile_publishes_and_reopens_actual_ordered_segment_artifacts`, `h16_core_two_trace_target_prints_backend_program_profile_rejection_before_reconstruction`, `h16_core_two_inspect_target_refuses_with_core_profile_before_target_read`, `h19_core_two_compile_call_refuses_before_deployment_read_or_emission`, `h18_core_two_compile_signed_target_is_unsupported_before_output_directory`, plus `SIGNED_TARGET`) and `fee_pool_component.rs` (`static_command`, `status_text`, `public_source_static_all_actions_and_separate_process_reopen_both_programs`, `signed_whole_program_rejects_real_mixed_payers_and_stale_inputs_publish_nothing`) preserves all Core CLI tests under `--no-default-features`. Note that `fn status_text` in `fee_pool_component.rs` (line 72) is only called by the two gated static-compile tests and must also be gated under `#[cfg(feature = "native")]`. The frozen financial/stage/logical-meter oracle requirements and no-native boundary test requirements are complete and non-tautological.

`RUST_GUIDELINES.md` subprocess exception and cross-directory fixture provenance (`RUST_GUIDELINES.md`): `RUST_GUIDELINES.md` currently forbids tests invoking the CLI binary (line 252) and reading files outside `crates/` (lines 227-229), whereas existing tests in `crates/mori/tests/` invoke `CARGO_BIN_EXE_mori` and read `../../models/core-stage-tests` (`stage_test_public.rs`), `../../../examples/core/continuations/...` (`core_continuations.rs`), and `../../examples/core/fee-pool` (`fee_pool_component.rs`, `core_test_report.rs`). The design properly records the narrow CLI subprocess boundary test exception (for frozen output/exit/I/O and feature availability, with no `--help` snapshots) and explicitly tracks the cross-directory fixture gap for resolution via `crates/fixtures/` copies with recorded digests or an explicit documented exception.
